stories.headline: Calls for action on derelict hotel site in Spalding
stories.brief: Residents and local observers are calling for progress regarding the future of a derelict hotel site in Spalding. Reports suggest that the current state of the property has led to demands for the location to be either fully developed or demolished. The site has been described as a "grot spot," prompting concerns about its impact on the local area. There is currently no word on potential redevelopment plans or a timeline for any work to take place at the location.

stories.headline: Drainage work to close Birchwood Street in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council is set to begin essential drainage work on Birchwood Street in King’s Lynn. Starting on or around Thursday, November 19, the project involves digging trial holes and is expected to last five days, with completion scheduled for November 25, weather permitting.

The road will be closed to traffic for the duration of the works. While access for residents and businesses will be maintained from one end of the street, there may be temporary restrictions directly outside individual properties. Motorists are being asked to remove all vehicles from parking areas along the road to ensure safety. Emergency services have been notified of the planned closure.

stories.headline: Peterborough hospital sleepout planned for Christmas appeal
stories.brief: Two people are preparing to take part in a sponsored sleepout at Peterborough City Hospital. The event is being held to raise funds for the hospital’s Christmas appeal. Further details regarding the date of the event or how members of the public can get involved have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Spalding salon celebrates 30th anniversary
stories.brief: A hair salon in Spalding is marking a significant milestone this week. The business is celebrating its 30th birthday and has issued a message of thanks to its loyal clients for their support over the last three decades.

stories.headline: Firefighters attend blaze at derelict building in March
stories.brief: Fire crews have been called to deal with a fire at a derelict building in the town of March. Emergency services attended the scene to tackle the blaze. No further details regarding the cause of the fire or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from November 2013 and 2014
stories.brief: We are taking a look back at stories from across the region during November in 2013 and 2014. Notable events included the 40th anniversary of the Dersingham Scout and Guide headquarters and the 50th anniversary of the North Lynn Methodist Church. In King’s Lynn, the first phase of the Hillington Square regeneration was completed, and the town saw the opening of The Gatehouse pub. Other highlights from the period included the Christmas lights switch-on, fundraising efforts at the Bespak factory for Movember, and the return of a restored World War I medal to a local family. Additionally, the Sandringham Flower Show announced a record donation of £50,000 to various charities.

stories.headline: Chatteris community archive marks two decades of history
stories.brief: The Chatteris community archive is celebrating a significant milestone this week, marking twenty years of operation. The local collection has grown to include 3,000 historic photographs, preserving the area's heritage for future generations. Residents interested in local history can explore the extensive archive, which has been documenting the town’s past for two decades.

stories.headline: Car fire reported on Lincoln Road in Peterborough
stories.brief: Emergency services have dealt with a vehicle fire on Lincoln Road in Peterborough. Footage circulating online shows the car engulfed in flames. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time. Motorists in the area are advised to remain aware of potential traffic disruption while the scene is cleared.

stories.headline: Long Sutton waste site operator fined £1 million
stories.brief: An operator of an illegal waste site in Long Sutton has been ordered to pay one million pounds in fines. The penalty follows legal action concerning the unauthorised management of waste at the location. No further details regarding the operator or the specific nature of the site have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police confirm deliberate fire at derelict Cambridgeshire hotel
stories.brief: Police have confirmed that a fire at a derelict hotel in Cambridgeshire was started deliberately. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the blaze. No further details regarding the location or the timing of the incident have been released at this stage. Residents are advised to monitor local updates as the investigation continues.

stories.headline: New management team takes over historic King’s Lynn pub
stories.brief:
The Lattice House on Chapel Street in King’s Lynn is under new management. Owner Daniel High has appointed Shannon Durrant to lead the historic venue, which dates back to the late 1400s. Mr Durrant, who has extensive experience in the West Norfolk hospitality sector, is leading a team of chefs and front-of-house staff.

The pub has introduced a new menu featuring pub classics, pizzas, and Thursday night curries, alongside a new cocktail selection. Future plans for the venue include the introduction of a gravity-fed bar for ales and beers. Mr Durrant says his goal is to create a welcoming atmosphere and build a sustainable business that the local community can be proud of.

stories.headline: Long Sutton headteacher defends school incentive scheme
stories.brief: The headteacher of a school in Long Sutton has spoken out in support of a new incentive programme. The initiative, which has been described as a "duvet day," has been introduced at the school to encourage attendance and engagement among pupils. While the scheme has attracted attention, the headteacher has defended the decision to implement the reward system. No further details regarding the specific criteria for the incentive or the school's broader attendance policy have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Financial boost for Chatteris Town FC
stories.brief: Chatteris Town Football Club has received a donation of £15,000. The funding was provided by a homebuilder based in Cambridgeshire.

stories.headline: Firework displays scheduled across West Norfolk this week
stories.brief:
Residents across West Norfolk have several firework displays to look forward to this week. Events begin on Thursday, November 5, at the North Wootton Scout and Guide Headquarters, with gates opening at 5pm. On Friday, November 6, King’s Lynn hosts the Fawkes in The Walks event, featuring live entertainment from 6pm and a choreographed display at 8pm.

The weekend continues on Saturday, November 7, with the Hunstanton and District Round Table’s 50th anniversary clifftop display, and a two-part event at the Denver playing fields. Those planning to attend should check local websites for ticket information and specific entry requirements, as arrangements vary between locations.

stories.headline: Second man sentenced following Peterborough robbery
stories.brief: A second man has been sent to prison for his involvement in a robbery in Peterborough. The incident left two teenage boys feeling extremely shaken. Legal proceedings have now concluded for the second individual involved in the case.

stories.headline: Number of Cambridgeshire police officers on barred list doubles
stories.brief: The number of Cambridgeshire Police officers added to the national barred list has doubled over the past year. According to figures reported by the Ely Standard, the total count of officers placed on the list has seen a significant increase compared to the previous twelve-month period. The barred list is used to prevent individuals from working in policing roles across the country following findings of gross misconduct.

stories.headline: New initiative aims to revitalise local market towns
stories.brief: A new plan has been launched to help bring market towns back to life. The initiative features the introduction of buskers to town centres as part of efforts to boost the local area. Further details on the scheme, reported by LincsOnline, suggest the move is intended to increase activity and footfall within these communities.

stories.headline: Fire crews tackle blaze at former March hotel
stories.brief: Emergency services are currently dealing with a significant fire at a former hotel in March. Reports indicate that the building is at risk of collapse following the blaze. Local residents are advised to be aware of the ongoing situation as crews work at the scene. Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Operatic and Dramatic Society stages The Addams Family Musical
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn Operatic and Dramatic Society, known as KLODS, recently performed The Addams Family Musical at the Peter Hopkins Hall at Springwood High School. The production, directed by Alex Kendal, featured a cast including Harry Bird as Gomez and Ellen Petterson-Brister as Morticia. Attendees praised the performance for its choreography, lighting, and humour, describing the show as being of West End quality. 

The society is expected to announce details regarding auditions and read-throughs for their upcoming productions on their official Facebook page soon.

stories.headline: Fire at derelict hotel in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Emergency services have attended a fire at a derelict former hotel in Cambridgeshire. The incident, which was reported by the Cambs Times, involved the abandoned building being engulfed by flames. No further details regarding the exact location or the cause of the fire have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Power restored following North Lynn building fire
stories.brief:
Four fire crews were called to a building blaze on Coulton Close in North Lynn yesterday evening. Firefighters from King’s Lynn, Terrington, and Sandringham attended the scene after the alarm was raised at 7:36pm. 

To ensure safety during the operation, UK Power Networks isolated electricity supplies to 108 households at 8:29pm. Power was successfully restored to all but one of those properties by 10:05pm. Crews remained on site until the incident was concluded at 1:51am this morning.

stories.headline: New community support hub opens in Peterborough
stories.brief: A new community support hub has officially opened its doors in Peterborough. The facility is now available to provide assistance to local residents. Further details regarding the services offered at the site have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Taylor Wimpey secures land for 80 new homes in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Housebuilder Taylor Wimpey has acquired a new site in Cambridgeshire. The company plans to construct a residential development consisting of 80 homes on the land. Further details regarding the specific location or the timeline for the project have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Firefighters respond to midnight blaze in Spalding
stories.brief: Emergency services were called to a house fire in Spalding during the early hours of this morning. Fire crews attended the scene at midnight to tackle the blaze. No further details regarding the cause of the fire or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Fire crews tackle blaze at former March hotel
stories.brief: Emergency services are currently dealing with a significant fire at a former hotel in March. Officials have warned that the building is at risk of collapse due to the severity of the blaze. Residents are advised to avoid the immediate area while fire crews work to bring the situation under control. There is no further information available at this time regarding the cause of the fire or any potential casualties.

stories.headline: Wisbech carpentry students build play kitchens for local playground
stories.brief:
Carpentry students from the College of West Anglia have completed a community project for the Wisbech Adventure Playground. Level 2 students William, Marc, Reece, and Noah designed and built two bespoke play kitchens using reclaimed wood. The finished items were presented to playground representative Violet Loveridge this week. 

Course lecturer Jamie Baker said the project allowed students to develop their skills while working sustainably. The new equipment is now available for children to use at The Spinney, with local officials praising the initiative for providing new opportunities for creative play. The project marks a successful collaboration between the college and the local community.

stories.headline: Series of convictions at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
A range of cases were heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last Thursday. Several individuals appeared before the bench for driving offences, including drink and drug-driving. Among those sentenced were Oliver Saunders of Stoke Ferry, who received a 12-month driving ban for being six times over the cocaine limit, and Kevin Sherman of Necton, who was disqualified for 15 months for drink-driving.

The court also dealt with various theft and public order offences. These included a shoplifting case involving 20 bottles of whisky, a man pleading guilty to cultivating cannabis, and a case involving threatening behaviour at a restaurant in King’s Lynn. Several defendants were issued fines and court costs, with some sentencing hearings adjourned until later this year.

stories.headline: New Ali G film released featuring Sacha Baron Cohen
stories.brief:
Sacha Baron Cohen has returned to the screen as his well-known character Ali G in the new film, Ali G: Who Iz I? The movie, which marks Baron Cohen’s directorial debut, follows the character as he travels to America to revive his television career after discovering his girlfriend is expecting a baby. 

The production features a mix of scripted scenes alongside the performer's signature hidden-camera encounters with members of the public. While reviews suggest the film’s narrative structure impacts the overall pacing, it continues to include moments of improvisation. The film also stars Morgana Robinson and Stewart Rodeheaver.

stories.headline: Power restored following North Lynn building fire
stories.brief:
Four fire crews were called to a building blaze on Coulton Close in North Lynn yesterday evening. Firefighters from King’s Lynn, Terrington, and Sandringham arrived at the scene following a report at 7:36pm. 

To ensure safety, UK Power Networks engineers isolated electricity supplies to 108 households at 8:29pm. Power was restored to all but one of those properties by 10:05pm. Crews remained on site using hose reel and main jets to tackle the fire, with the incident officially concluded at 1:51am this morning.

stories.headline: Six fireworks displays planned for Peterborough this Bonfire Night
stories.brief: Residents in the Peterborough area have six different fireworks displays to choose from this Bonfire Night. Details of the various events have been published by the Peterborough Telegraph, offering local people a range of options for the upcoming celebrations. Those planning to attend are encouraged to check local listings for specific timings and venue information.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire households to receive £100 energy payment
stories.brief: Households across Cambridgeshire are set to receive a one-off energy payment of £100. The funding is being distributed to residents in each area of the county to assist with rising costs. Further details regarding the eligibility criteria and the distribution process for these payments are expected to be released shortly. Residents are advised to monitor local updates for information on how this support will be provided in their specific district.

stories.headline: E-scooter battery sparks house fire in Spalding
stories.brief: Fire crews have confirmed that a blaze at a home in Spalding was started by an e-scooter battery. Emergency services attended the scene following the incident, which has prompted reminders about the potential risks associated with charging these devices. No further details regarding the extent of the damage or any injuries have been released at this time. Residents are being urged to ensure they follow safety guidelines when charging lithium-ion batteries for e-scooters and e-bikes.

stories.headline: Fire reported at derelict hotel in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Emergency services have been called to a fire at a derelict hotel in a Cambridgeshire town. The incident was reported by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. No further details regarding the location or the extent of the damage have been released at this time. Residents are advised to stay clear of the area while crews manage the situation.

stories.headline: Home Office to proceed with asylum accommodation in Leverington
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has expressed deep concern after the Home Office confirmed plans to use Roman Court in Leverington as asylum accommodation. The site is intended to house 26 women and babies. The council had previously raised objections regarding public safety, community cohesion, and the suitability of the location. 

The Home Office stated that the site will only become operational once it meets all necessary legal, safety, and regulatory requirements. This decision follows recent public protests and a fire at the property, which remains under police investigation. Officials from the Home Office are scheduled to meet with council and police representatives tomorrow to discuss the matter further.

stories.headline: New supermarket and care home proposed for King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Plans have been submitted to West Norfolk Council for a new development on the outskirts of King’s Lynn. The proposal for land off Edward Benefer Way includes a new Lidl supermarket and a three-storey care home featuring 66 bedrooms. 

The site, located near the Wootton Grange housing development, would also include electric vehicle charging points and dedicated parking for both facilities. Developers state the project aims to provide specialist care for older people and increase retail choice for the local community. The application is currently awaiting consideration by the council.

stories.headline: Police investigate meat theft in Spalding
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating the theft of meat from a shop in Spalding. Officers are currently looking into the incident, which was reported at a store within the town. No further details regarding the items taken or potential suspects have been released at this stage. Anyone with information that could assist the investigation is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Whittlesey’s Manor Leisure Centre faces potential demolition
stories.brief: New development plans for Whittlesey could see the total demolition of the Manor Leisure Centre. The proposal is currently under consideration as part of a wider scheme for the area. No further details regarding the timeline or potential replacements for the facility have been released at this stage. Residents are advised to monitor local planning updates for any future developments regarding the site.

stories.headline: Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training facility in South Lynn
stories.brief:
A new £600,000 specialist training facility is planned for the South Lynn fire station. The project is being funded through a joint investment of £300,000 each from Norfolk County Council and West Norfolk Council. The facility will be built on vacant land behind the station and is designed to provide realistic training for complex emergencies, including road traffic collisions and rescues at height.

Construction is expected to begin next year, subject to planning consent and site surveys. Currently, crews must travel to North Lynn for essential training. This new development aims to keep firefighters closer to their station, reducing travel time and ensuring crews remain available to respond to emergency calls across West Norfolk.

stories.headline: Peterborough death notices for October 2026
stories.brief: The Peterborough Telegraph has published its list of death notices for the month of October 2026. The latest round-up includes the names of 19 individuals who have recently passed away. Families and friends wishing to view the full details of these notices can find them in the pages of the Peterborough Telegraph.

stories.headline: Further delay for council reform plans in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
stories.brief: A decision regarding major structural reforms for councils in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough has been postponed once again. The proposed changes, which would impact local government operations across the region, remain on hold following the latest delay. No new date for a final decision has been announced.

stories.headline: Positive coronavirus tests confirmed at Lincolnshire school
stories.brief: A school in Lincolnshire has reported a number of positive coronavirus cases. The institution confirmed that several individuals have tested positive for the virus. No further details regarding the specific location of the school or the number of people affected have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn students honoured for STEM achievements
stories.brief:
Around 50 students from Springwood High School in King’s Lynn have been recognised for their success in science, technology, engineering, and maths. Pupils from years 8 to 12 attended a special celebration evening to receive awards and certificates for their work over the past academic year. 

The event highlighted achievements from both school and regional competitions. Guest speaker Professor Abby Onencan from the University of East Anglia addressed the attendees, discussing the importance of the field. Organisers say the ceremony aimed to celebrate the contributions of the students and demonstrate that STEM subjects are accessible to everyone at the school.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend house fire in Lincolnshire village
stories.brief: Emergency crews are currently at the scene of a house fire in a Lincolnshire village. Emergency services remain in attendance at the property. No further details regarding the location or any potential casualties have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Proposed Fenland wind farm could power 100,000 homes
stories.brief: A new wind farm project has been proposed for the Fenland area. According to reports from the Cambs Times, the development has the potential to generate enough electricity to supply more than 100,000 homes. No further details regarding the specific location or timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn care worker wins community award for second year
stories.brief:
A member of staff at King’s Lynn Residential Care Home has been honoured for her work in the community. Jo Taylor received the Family and Community Engagement Award at the recent Black Swan Care Awards, marking the second consecutive year she has won the title. 

Ms Taylor was nominated for the award by her colleagues, the Royal British Legion, and local residents. Home manager Jodi Collins praised Ms Taylor’s dedication to creating meaningful experiences for those in her care and maintaining strong community connections. Following the ceremony, staff and residents at the home held celebrations to mark her achievement.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated in League Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United’s women’s team has been knocked out of the League Cup following a defeat against Norwich City. The match ended in a four-nil victory for the Norwich side. The result was confirmed by Norwich City Football Club.

stories.headline: District council seeks greater role in social care
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council is calling for more responsibility regarding social care services. According to reports from the Local Government Chronicle, the authority is seeking a larger role in the management and delivery of these provisions. No further details have been provided regarding how these changes might be implemented or the potential impact on local residents. We will continue to monitor this story as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Improvements underway at local business park
stories.brief: Work is currently taking place to refresh a business park in the region. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, the site is undergoing a spruce up. No further details regarding the scale of the project or the specific location have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: March business claims lack of belief hinders black entrepreneurs
stories.brief: A business based in March has highlighted challenges facing black entrepreneurs. The firm, known as Rayo, suggests that a lack of belief is currently holding back black business owners. No further details regarding the company’s specific experiences or proposed solutions were provided in the report.

stories.headline: Festive events announced for True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum
stories.brief:
True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum in King’s Lynn is hosting a series of Christmas events following a grant of over £2,500. The ‘Reel Bright Idea’ project includes a free Dickensian trail launching in November, alongside an exhibition on the history of Christmas tree decorations. 

Families can also enjoy free yoga classes, craft sessions, and a Christmas fair. Other highlights include a carol concert at All Saints’ Church on December 9 and evening museum openings in mid-December. Many activities are free, though some require advance booking. For full details on the schedule or to reserve a place, visit the True’s Yard website, call 01553 770479, or email info@truesyard.co.uk.

stories.headline: Obituary notice for Rex Richardson of Long Sutton
stories.brief: An obituary has been published for Rex Richardson, a resident of Long Sutton in Lincolnshire. The notice, which appeared in the Spalding Guardian, confirms that Mr Richardson passed away in 2020. No further details regarding his life or funeral arrangements have been provided in the report.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over proposed Chatteris energy plant
stories.brief: Residents in Chatteris have expressed concerns regarding a proposed energy plant for the town. Reports indicate that local people are worried about the potential for unpleasant odours resulting from the development. The plans for the new facility have been highlighted by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News.

stories.headline: Future of Queen Elizabeth Hospital services to be discussed
stories.brief:
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group Board is meeting on Monday, November 2, to discuss a new clinical strategy for the region. The board will review a "Case for Change" document, which examines how healthcare services might develop over the coming decades.

This follows public concern regarding reports that accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn could face closure. However, the hospital group has stressed that no decisions have been made. They state the meeting is not a consultation on service changes, but rather the start of a conversation about how to improve care while addressing staffing pressures and changing population needs.

stories.headline: Age UK highlights impact of Cambridgeshire handyperson service cuts
stories.brief: Age UK has raised concerns regarding the decision by Cambridgeshire County Council to withdraw funding for its handyperson service. The service, which provided practical support to residents, will no longer receive financial backing from the local authority. The charity has highlighted the potential impact this change will have on those who relied on the assistance provided. No further details regarding the timeline for the service closure or potential alternative support options have been released by the council at this stage.

stories.headline: Waterstones King’s Lynn names new Book of the Week
stories.brief:
Waterstones in King’s Lynn has announced its latest Book of the Week. The store is currently highlighting The Wax Child by author Olga Ravn. The novel is a reimagining of a 17th-century Danish witch trial, exploring themes of persecution and suspicion. 

The shop has also released its current top ten chart. Other titles featuring in the list include The Case of the Christmas Card by Elly Griffiths, Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman, and Quirky King’s Lynn by Bill Lovelock. Readers can find more information on these titles by visiting the King’s Lynn branch.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated by Luton Town
stories.brief: Peterborough United have suffered a defeat in their latest League One fixture. The team lost 2-0 to Luton Town. Highlights of the match have been made available via Sky Sports.

stories.headline: Ely restaurant receives praise for burgers
stories.brief: A local restaurant in Ely has been highlighted for its food, with a recent report describing the establishment as serving the best burgers in Cambridgeshire. The recognition comes from the Cambs Times, which featured the venue in a recent article. Residents looking for highly-rated dining options in the city may wish to take note of the positive review.

stories.headline: Contractors appointed for bus shelter repairs
stories.brief: Maintenance work is set to take place on a local bus shelter. Contractors have been called in to carry out repairs to the structure. No further details regarding the location or the timeline for the work have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Former March mayor expresses interest in buying town hall
stories.brief: A former mayor of March has announced an intention to purchase the town hall. The news was reported by the BBC. No further details regarding the potential sale or the identity of the former official have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Heacham man fined for cannabis possession in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A 46-year-old man from Heacham has been fined after being caught with cannabis in King’s Lynn town centre. Samuel Wright, of Station Road, was arrested on the evening of October 4 following reports regarding his behaviour on Littleport Street. Police officers searched Mr Wright and discovered 16 grams of the Class B drug in his pocket.

Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Wright entered a guilty plea. The court heard that the defendant, who works as a grounds worker, had not committed an offence in the last five years. He was ordered to pay a total of £1,093, which includes a £720 fine, a £288 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

stories.headline: Nominations open for fifth annual Fenland Citizen Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now open for the fifth annual Fenland Citizen Business Awards. Businesses, individuals, and charities from across the district are invited to enter across eight categories, including Business of the Year, Employer of the Year, and Best New Start-Up. 

The awards ceremony will take place on Friday, March 19, 2027, at the Wisbech St Mary Sports and Community Centre. Those wishing to submit an entry can find full criteria and nomination details on the Fenland Business Awards website. The deadline for all entries is 5pm on Wednesday, January 6.

stories.headline: Government cancels £300 million A10 upgrade scheme
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade the A10 between Ely and Cambridge have been cancelled. The government has confirmed it is pulling the plug on the £300 million project. The scheme, which aimed to improve the route between the two locations, will no longer go ahead.

stories.headline: Spalding recycling firm seeks permission to remain at current site
stories.brief: A recycling business based in Spalding has submitted a formal application to continue operating from its existing location. The proposal, reported by LincsOnline, seeks official approval for the company to remain at its current site. No further details regarding the application or the specific location have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: New visitor and gift shop planned for March geese
stories.brief: A new visitor and gift shop is set to open in March, dedicated to the town's geese. The project aims to provide a dedicated space for those interested in the local wildlife. Further details regarding the opening date or the specific location of the new facility have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Wisbech cinema to host screening of new British documentary
stories.brief:
A new British feature documentary, The Fastest Bicycle, is coming to The Light Cinema in Wisbech next month. Directed by double BAFTA-winner Michael B. Clifford, the film follows a London-based team attempting to compete in the World Human Powered Speed Challenge in Nevada. The documentary chronicles the group's seven-year journey, detailing the various technical and personal challenges they faced while preparing for the event.

The screening is scheduled for Thursday, November 12, at 7.30 pm. The film is dedicated to the late designer Mike Burrows and explores themes of perseverance and community within the world of high-speed cycling. Tickets are available for the local showing as part of a nationwide release.

stories.headline: Sentencing delayed for King's Lynn sexual assault offender
stories.brief:
The sentencing of 21-year-old Callum Howe has been postponed. Mr Howe, of Woolstencroft Avenue in King’s Lynn, previously pleaded guilty to a sexual assault that occurred in the town on February 8. He was scheduled to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court this past Thursday, but requested a delay to seek legal representation.

The court has rescheduled the hearing for December 15. Mr Howe has been released on conditional bail and is prohibited from contacting the victim.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn concert celebrates cultural diversity through music and dance
stories.brief:
A sold-out concert at the King’s Lynn Masonic Centre on Sunday, October 25, showcased a blend of Indian classical and Western artistic traditions. Organised by Sursarang Arts, the "Music Beyond Borders" event featured performances ranging from Kathak and Flamenco dancing to violin and vocal collaborations. The Mayor of King’s Lynn and West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, was among the capacity audience. 

Directors Dr Prabir Mitra and Sanjukta Mitra hosted the evening to highlight how the arts can bridge different cultures. The programme included an instrumental duet by visiting artist Pandit Pallab Bandyopadhyay and concluded with a grand finale involving all performers. The organisers hope the event will foster greater cultural appreciation across the region.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Under-21s defeated in Newcastle
stories.brief: Peterborough United’s Under-21 side suffered a defeat on the road yesterday. The young Posh squad were beaten 2-0 by Newcastle United’s Under-21 team.

stories.headline: Woman dies following Sutton Bridge collision
stories.brief: A woman in her eighties has died following a road traffic collision in Sutton Bridge, Lincolnshire. Police have confirmed the fatality occurred in the village, though no further details regarding the circumstances of the incident or the vehicles involved have been released at this time. Authorities are currently managing the situation.

stories.headline: Met Office weather update for Whittlesey
stories.brief: The Met Office has issued a weather update for the Whittlesey area of Cambridgeshire. Residents are advised to check the latest forecasts for any potential changes in local conditions. Further information regarding the current outlook is available through official Met Office channels.

stories.headline: Search underway for unclaimed £1M Lotto prize in Fenland
stories.brief:
A search is underway for a National Lottery player in Fenland who has won £1 million but has yet to come forward. The winning ticket was purchased for the draw held on Saturday, October 17. The successful numbers were 4, 9, 15, 32, 38, 42, with 2 as the Bonus Ball.

Lottery operator Allwyn is urging residents to check their tickets, including those kept in cars or kitchen drawers. The winner has until midnight on April 15, 2027, to claim the prize. Anyone who believes they have the winning ticket should contact the National Lottery line on 0333 2345050 or email help@national-lottery.co.uk. If the prize remains unclaimed, the money will be donated to National Lottery-funded projects.

stories.headline: Wisbech students win national award for hedgehog conservation business
stories.brief: Three construction students from the College of West Anglia in Wisbech have achieved national success in the Peter Jones Foundation’s Tycoon Enterprise Competition. Finn McAuley, Marc Watson, and Erikas Rimkus, known as The Fabulous Baker’s Trio, secured joint first place in the Business for Good category. The students were recognised for their project, which involves building hedgehog houses to provide shelter for local wildlife. The enterprise also supported the charity Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel through fundraising efforts. College staff praised the trio for their hard work and dedication, noting that the project successfully combined practical construction skills with a commitment to environmental conservation.

stories.headline: Calls for parking policy review after disabled shoppers face fines
stories.brief:
A Dersingham resident is calling for supermarkets to offer more flexibility to disabled customers after receiving multiple parking fines in King’s Lynn. Amanda Archer, who cares for her mother, Jill Garratt, says the pair struggle to complete their shopping within standard time limits due to mobility issues. 

Ms Archer received a seventy-pound charge after exceeding the ninety-minute limit at the Gaywood Aldi, and a previous sixty-pound fine at Home Bargains. Parkingeye, which manages the Aldi site, confirmed that Ms Archer’s recent fine has been cancelled following an appeal. The company stated that their system is designed to identify overstays, and they encourage motorists to submit mitigating circumstances through their formal appeals process.

stories.headline: Norwich City to face Peterborough United in League Cup
stories.brief: Norwich City Women are set to take on Peterborough United in an upcoming League Cup fixture. The match, hosted by Norwich City Football Club, will see the two sides compete for a place in the next round of the competition. Supporters are advised to check official club channels for kick-off times and ticket availability as the teams prepare for this regional encounter.

stories.headline: Roadworks scheduled for A17 between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens should prepare for disruption this weekend as surfacing works begin on the A17. Lincolnshire County Council has confirmed that the maintenance project will take place on the stretch of road located between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these improvements are carried out.

stories.headline: March café hosts exhibition for artists with learning disabilities
stories.brief: The Hot Pots Café in March is currently hosting an exhibition featuring artwork created by people with learning disabilities and autism. The display is supported by Cambridgeshire County Council. Residents are invited to visit the café to view the work produced by these local artists.

stories.headline: Wisbech’s Luxe Cinema reopens today
stories.brief:
The Luxe Cinema on Alexandra Road in Wisbech is welcoming customers back this afternoon. The venue had been closed since earlier this week due to what management described as unexpected circumstances. 

In a social media update posted this morning, a spokesperson confirmed that the cinema is now ready to resume screenings. The closure was necessary while the business renegotiated its insurance policy, a process that has now been resolved. Doors are scheduled to open from 1pm today.

stories.headline: Swaffham paramedic shortlisted for national Morning Hero award
stories.brief:
A Swaffham-based paramedic is in the running to be named Britain’s Morning Hero. Carl Smith, who is well known in the West Norfolk area, has been named as one of five finalists in the nationwide competition. Mr Smith balances his career with the East of England Ambulance Service and Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service alongside driving a school bus each morning. 

The award celebrates individuals who show dedication to their local communities. Mr Smith, who was awarded the British Empire Medal in the 2024 New Year Honours, is now calling for public support. Voting is open until midnight on November 10 via the Tiptree website, with the winner to be announced later this month.

stories.headline: Emergency lock closures leave boaters stranded in March
stories.brief: Boaters are currently unable to move through March following the introduction of emergency lock closures. The restrictions have left vessels marooned in the area. No further details regarding the cause of the closures or when the locks might reopen have been provided at this stage. Those planning to travel through the town by water are advised to be aware of the disruption.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn’s dark history explored this Halloween
stories.brief:
As Halloween approaches, King’s Lynn is being highlighted for its centuries-old history of folklore and paranormal legends. The town’s past includes the 1590 execution of Margaret Read, who was burned at the stake in the Tuesday Market Place after being convicted of witchcraft. 

Beyond historical trials, the town is associated with numerous ghost stories, including reports of spectral sightings at True’s Yard Museum and the Duke’s Head Hotel. Local tales also feature a medieval exorcist’s former home and a legend involving a devil’s hoofprint left in the town’s cobbles. These stories continue to shape the town’s identity as it marks the annual celebration of Halloween on October 31.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough council restructuring delayed
stories.brief: Plans for a shake-up of local government across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough have been pushed back once again. The proposed changes to the structure of the councils in the region are facing further delays, according to reports. No new timeline for the implementation of these adjustments has been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: South Cambridgeshire residents voice East West Rail concerns
stories.brief: People living in South Cambridgeshire have expressed concerns regarding the proposed East West Rail project. The development, which aims to improve rail connectivity across the region, has prompted local residents to speak out about the scheme. Further details on the nature of these objections have not been disclosed at this time.

stories.headline: Missing woman located safe and well
stories.brief: A woman reported missing has been found safe and well. The news follows a public appeal for information regarding her whereabouts. No further details have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech’s Luxe Cinema closes temporarily
stories.brief: The Luxe Cinema on Alexandra Road in Wisbech has announced an immediate closure. Management confirmed the venue is shut until further notice, citing unexpected circumstances. In a statement posted on social media, the cinema said it intends to contact all affected guests as soon as possible. Staff have thanked the public for their support and understanding during this time. No further details regarding the reason for the closure or a potential reopening date have been provided.

stories.headline: Marshland councillor shares budget concerns and Remembrance plans
stories.brief:
Reform UK county councillor for Marshland North, Julian Kirk, has criticised the recent national budget. Cllr Kirk described the current system as broken, citing concerns over high taxation, rising unemployment, and unsustainable employment costs for businesses. He argued that welfare spending should be redirected towards national defence, citing the current global climate.

Looking ahead, Cllr Kirk is preparing for upcoming Remembrance commemorations. He is scheduled to lay wreaths in both King’s Lynn and Norwich to mark Armistice Day and Remembrance Sunday. Additionally, the councillor commented on potential plans for a Norfolk and Suffolk mayor in 2028, expressing scepticism regarding the promise of extra government funding.

stories.headline: New gym equipment installed at Fenland leisure centres
stories.brief:
Council-owned leisure centres in Chatteris, March, Whittlesey, and Wisbech are receiving a significant upgrade to their gym facilities. Fenland District Council has invested in new equipment, which is now being installed at the George Campbell Leisure Centre in March. 

To facilitate these improvements, gyms at other sites will close for three days each. Chatteris Leisure Centre closes from November 2 to 5, followed by the Hudson Leisure Centre in Wisbech from November 9 to 12. Finally, the Manor Leisure Centre in Whittlesey will be closed from November 17 to 20. During these periods, swimming pools and fitness classes will remain open as usual. The Hudson Leisure Centre will also gain a new dedicated space for dynamic workouts.

stories.headline: West Norfolk students showcase dance talent in new competition
stories.brief:
Students from four West Norfolk Academies Trust schools have taken part in a new dance competition held at Springwood High School. Thirty-eight pupils from years seven to thirteen, representing schools in King’s Lynn, Hunstanton, Terrington St Clement, and West Walton, demonstrated their technical skills and choreography. 

Participants were required to choreograph their own routines and select their own music for the event. The competition featured solo and group categories across Key Stages 3 and 4. Organisers hope the successful event will help raise the profile of dance across the Trust and lead to further projects in the future. All competitors received certificates, with trophies awarded to the winners in each category.

stories.headline: Bee-friendly roofs approved for bus stops
stories.brief: Plans have been approved to install mini-gardens on the roofs of bus stops. The initiative aims to support local bee populations by creating new habitats within the urban environment. The project, which was reported by the BBC, will see greenery planted atop existing bus shelter structures. No further details regarding the specific locations or the timeline for these installations have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire local government reorganisation delayed
stories.brief: Plans to reorganise local government in Cambridgeshire have been pushed back once again. The proposed changes are facing criticism, with some describing the situation as a political merry-go-round. No new timeline for the reorganisation has been confirmed following the latest setback.

stories.headline: New principal appointed at secondary school
stories.brief: A new principal has been appointed to lead a secondary school in the region. The school, which has been described as troubled, will see a change in leadership following the announcement. Further details regarding the identity of the new principal or the specific school involved have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: Nominations open for fifth annual Fenland Citizen Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now open for the fifth annual Fenland Citizen Business Awards. Businesses, individuals, and charities from across the district are invited to enter across eight categories, including Business of the Year, Employer of the Year, and Best New Start-Up. 

The awards aim to highlight local innovation and success stories. Entries must be submitted by 5pm on Wednesday, January 6. The winners will be announced during a black-tie event held at the Wisbech St Mary Sports and Community Centre on Friday, March 19, 2027. Further details regarding entry criteria and how to nominate can be found on the Fenland Business Awards website.

stories.headline: Downham Market toddler stars in national swimming campaign
stories.brief:
A three-year-old from Downham Market is helping to front a new national initiative from Swim England. Phoebe Stoves and her grandmother, Gill, are featured in the ‘Love Swimming’ campaign, which highlights the benefits of pool sessions for families. 

Phoebe began lessons in April and has since grown in confidence after initially feeling nervous. The campaign, supported by Alive West Norfolk, encourages families to start swimming lessons this autumn. Research cited by the organisation suggests that most children show improved water confidence after only a few sessions. Those interested in finding local classes can visit the Swim England website at swimming.org/poolfinder for more information.

stories.headline: Ely MP criticises Autumn Budget
stories.brief: The Member of Parliament for Ely has expressed dissatisfaction with the government’s recent Autumn Budget. In comments reported by the Ely Standard, the local representative described the financial plans as not being bold enough to meet current requirements. No further details regarding specific policies or the MP's alternative proposals were provided in the report.

stories.headline: Popeyes to open new restaurant in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new Popeyes restaurant is coming to King’s Lynn. The fried chicken chain has confirmed it will take over the former Pizza Hut site at the Campbells Meadow retail park. While an official opening date has not yet been announced, the company says the new location will feature both dine-in facilities and park-and-serve bays for online orders. 

The restaurant will serve the brand’s signature Louisiana-style chicken and buttermilk biscuits. Popeyes UK chief executive Tom Crowley said the company is looking forward to bringing its flavours to the local community. The chain, which was founded in 1972, has been expanding across the UK since 2021.

stories.headline: England Men prepare for Rugby League World Cup clash against PNG
stories.brief: The England Men’s rugby league team is looking to secure a decisive victory in their upcoming third match of the RLWC26 tournament. They are set to face Papua New Guinea in a game that forms part of the current World Cup schedule. Fans of the sport can expect a competitive encounter as England aims to build on their performance in the competition so far.

stories.headline: Local geese to feature in new calendar
stories.brief: A group of geese known for their celebrity status are set to be featured in an upcoming calendar. The birds, which have gained local attention, will be the subject of the new publication. Further details regarding the release or where the calendar will be available have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: Further delays announced for Cambridgeshire local government shakeup
stories.brief:
Plans to reorganise local government in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough have faced further delays. The government has confirmed that the transition process, which aimed to replace existing district and county councils with new unitary authorities, will not proceed at this time. 

While other regions have been selected to move forward, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough remain under review, with a further update expected by Christmas. The government has pledged £500,000 in transition funding to the area to help manage the costs of ongoing uncertainty. Local leaders have criticised the delay, describing the situation as a source of frustration for council staff, businesses, and residents who are seeking clarity on the future of local public services.

stories.headline: Police investigate jewellery theft in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Police are investigating a burglary at a town centre business in King’s Lynn. Officers were called to a premises near the junction with Albert Street shortly after 5:30 this morning. 

It is believed that jewellery was stolen during the incident. A police cordon was established at the scene earlier today to allow for an investigation, with crime scene investigators also in attendance. West Norfolk Police confirmed the activity on social media to keep the local community informed. Anyone with information regarding the burglary is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Four planning applications submitted for Ely area
stories.brief: Four new planning proposals have been submitted for sites in and around Ely. Each of the applications concerns locations that are either designated conservation areas or involve listed buildings. Local authorities are now reviewing the plans to determine their impact on the historic character of these sites. Further details regarding the specific nature of these developments and their exact locations can be found via the Ely Standard.

stories.headline: Opposition grows to proposed West Norfolk solar and data centre project
stories.brief: Residents are voicing concerns over a proposed development in West Norfolk, which includes a 1,300MW solar farm and an artificial intelligence data centre. The project is planned for the villages of Tilney St Lawrence, Barton Bendish, and Fincham. Critics argue that the solar farm is intended to power the data centre rather than provide renewable energy for the local area, and have raised concerns regarding the loss of agricultural land. Opponents are calling on local councillors and MPs to join together in opposing the plans.
